system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Bramley Lane Allotment Association rules (adopted October 2025). Rent is £64 for a full plot and £36 for a half plot, due by 1 October; over-65s and people on means-tested benefits pay half, and non-payment by 31 October brings a notice to quit. At least 75% of a plot must be cultivated in the March–October season, with inspections in April, June and August; a non-cultivation notice gives 28 days to improve and a second in one year can mean termination. Any plot holder may put up a shed of up to 6 × 4 ft and a greenhouse of up to 8 × 6 ft without permission, sited at the north end. No overnight stays or more than 5 litres of petrol. Trough water runs from April to October; no hoses or sprinklers. Bonfires are allowed for dry, untreated plant material and must be attended and fully put out before leaving. The Association maintains all paths, the car park, hedges and the communal compost bays through working parties. Up to six hens (no cockerels) and rabbits are allowed with permission. Fruit trees must be on dwarf rootstock and under 2.5 m. Metaldehyde slug pellets are banned. Visitors, children and dogs must be controlled. One month's notice to leave; no rent refunds; clear the plot within 28 days.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
BRAMLEY LANE ALLOTMENT ASSOCIATION — RULES FOR PLOT HOLDERS (adopted at the AGM, 18 October 2025)

1. Rent. Annual rent is £64 for a full plot (250 m²) and £36 for a half plot (125 m²), payable by 1 October each year for the year beginning that day. Plot holders aged 65 or over, or in receipt of a means-tested benefit, pay 50% of the standard rent on providing evidence. Rent not paid by 31 October will result in a notice to quit.

2. Cultivation. At least 75% of each plot must be under cultivation, with crops, fruit bushes or flowers, at all times during the growing season (March to October). Paths, sheds, compost areas and ponds do not count as cultivated. The committee inspects plots in April, June and August. A plot holder who receives a non-cultivation notice has 28 days to bring the plot up to standard; a second notice in the same year may result in termination.

3. Structures. On full plots, one shed of no more than 6 ft × 4 ft and one greenhouse of no more than 8 ft × 6 ft may be erected without permission, provided they are sited at the northern end of the plot. On half plots, any shed or greenhouse, of any size, requires the prior written permission of the committee. Structures must not be used for overnight stays or for storing petrol in quantities above 5 litres.

4. Water. Water is available from troughs from 1 April to 31 October. Hosepipes and sprinklers may not be used at any time. Watering cans must be filled by dipping in the trough; do not wash produce or tools in the troughs.

5. Bonfires. Bonfires are permitted only between 1 November and 28 February, and only for dry, untreated plant material. They must be attended at all times and fully extinguished before leaving. No bonfires are permitted at any other time of year.

6. Paths and boundaries. The grass path between two adjoining plots must be kept mown and clear by the two plot holders on either side, each being responsible for the half nearest their plot. The main site paths, the car park, perimeter hedges and the communal compost bays are maintained by the Association through working parties.

7. Livestock. Up to six hens may be kept on a full plot with the committee's written permission. Cockerels are not permitted. Rabbits may be kept for meat or as pets with permission. No other livestock may be kept.

8. Trees. Fruit trees must be on dwarfing rootstocks and must not exceed 2.5 metres in height. Other trees may not be planted.

9. Chemicals. The use of slug pellets containing metaldehyde is banned. Other pesticides must be stored in their original containers in a locked box.

10. Conduct. Plot holders are responsible for the behaviour of their visitors. Children must be supervised at all times. Dogs must be kept on a lead.

11. Termination. Plot holders wishing to give up a plot should give one month's notice to the Secretary. No rent is refunded. All structures and rubbish must be removed within 28 days of the tenancy ending, unless the incoming holder agrees to take them on.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. I rent a half plot. Can I put up a 6 ft × 4 ft shed without asking anyone?
2. What is the annual rent for a full plot?
3. Can I burn a pile of dry bean haulms on my plot in July?
4. The grass path between my plot and my neighbour's is knee-high. Whose job is it to mow it?
response:
Answers come from the rules document itself. My earlier notes were wrong on three of these points, so I've flagged where they differed.

**1. Half plot: can you put up a 6 × 4 ft shed without asking? No.**
Rule 3 lets holders of **full** plots put up a shed (up to 6 × 4 ft) and a greenhouse (up to 8 × 6 ft) without permission, at the northern end. On **half plots, any shed or greenhouse of any size needs the committee's prior written permission.** Get written approval before you build. *(My notes wrongly said any plot holder could do this.)*

**2. Annual rent for a full plot: £64.**
It's due by 1 October for the year starting that day (Rule 1). If you're 65 or over, or on a means-tested benefit, you pay 50% (£32) once you provide evidence. Rent not paid by 31 October leads to a notice to quit.

**3. Burning dry bean haulms in July? No.**
Rule 5 allows bonfires **only between 1 November and 28 February**, and only for dry, untreated plant material. July is outside that window, so compost the haulms or keep them until November. A winter bonfire must be attended at all times and fully put out before you leave. *(My notes left out the seasonal limit.)*

**4. Who mows the overgrown grass path between you and your neighbour? Both of you.**
Under Rule 6, the grass path between two adjoining plots is kept mown and clear by the two plot holders on either side. **Each of you is responsible for the half nearest your own plot.** The Association's working parties only look after the main site paths, the car park, perimeter hedges and the communal compost bays. *(My notes wrongly said the Association maintains all paths.)*
